Hello everyone. In this lecture, we will learn the fundamentals of a database management system, often abbreviated as dbms.
We will cover databases, relational tables, keys, normalization, structured query language, and transactions These ideas help applications or information correctly and retrieve it efficiently.
A database is an organized collection of related data For example, a university may store student details, course information, faculty records,.
and elimination results in a database A database management system is software used to create, read, update, and manage data.
And mammals include mySQL, postcurSQL, and Oracle database The database contains the data, the management system provides tools and rules for working with it.
In a relational database, information is arranged in tables A table contains rows and columns Each row represents one record, and each column represents an attribute.
A student table might contain student ID, name, email address, and department ID The table schema describes its columns and the kinds of values they can store.
keys help identify records and connect tables A primary key uniquely identifies each row It must be unique and cannot be held.
A foreign key refers to a key in another table, creating a relationship between the two tables For example, department ID in the student table can reference department ID in a department table.
This connection helps maintain referential integrity A candidate key is a minimal set of attributes that can uniquely identify a record.
One candidate key is chosen as the primary key Other candidate keys are called alternate keys A composite key uses two or more columns together.
In an enrollment table, student ID, and course ID may form a composite key Because a student can enroll in many courses, and a course can have many students.
Next, let us discuss normalization Normalization organizes tables to reduce unnecessary duplication and prevent insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.
First normal form requires each field to contain a single value rather than repeating list Second normal form requires first normal form.
and removes partial dependencies on part of a composite candidate key Third normal form requires second normal form, and removes transitive dependencies of non-key attributes.
Unkey, for instance, instead of repeating a department name for every student Store departments in a separate department table.
and reference M using department ID This reduces duplicated data, and makes updates more consistent When related information is needed from separate tables, SQL joins can combine the matching rows.
Structured query language, or SQL is used to query and modify relational data The select statement retrieves rows, insert adds a record, update changes existing values, and delete removes records.
where clause filters rows according to a condition, while ORDER BY sort the results An inner join returns rows with matching values in both tables.
A left join returns every row from the left table, and includes matching information from the right table when available.
joins commonly use primary key and foreign key relationships A transaction is a logical unit of database work.
Imagine transferring money between two bank accounts One operation subtracts money from the sender, and another adds it to the receiver.
If only one operation succeeds, the records become inconsistent A transaction groups these operations so they can be handled together.
Reliable transactions follow four important properties Atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability Atomicity means all operations in the transaction happen, or none of them do.
Consistency means the transaction preserves database rules, and constraints Isolation controls how concurrent transactions affect one another Durability means that after a transaction commits, its changes persist according to the database's recovery guarantees.
Commit confirms a transaction, while rollback cancels and committed changes Database systems also use locks and other concurrency control techniques.
To coordinate simultaneous access and protect shared data To summarize, database stores organized information Database management system controls access to it.
Relational tables organize records, keys connect related tables Normalization reduces redundancy, SQL queries, and changes data And transactions protect reliable updates.
These concepts work together Godtable design makes data consistent Keys establish relationships, joins retrieve related information, and transaction properties help.
Preserve correctness when failures or concurrent operations occur.
